subject: botany_2
question_text: What is meant by transport saturation? How does it influence facilitated diffusion?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.39, printed question 60. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR, corrected on this card: the book answers the second half with "Transport saturation INCREASES the facilitated diffusion." That is backwards. Once every carrier protein is occupied the rate cannot rise any further — saturation sets a CEILING, and that ceiling is exactly what distinguishes facilitated diffusion from simple diffusion, whose rate keeps climbing with concentration. The card writes it correctly and records the book's printed position here.

insider_note: This is the one question in the chapter where the guide's own answer is wrong. Saturation LIMITS the rate; it does not increase it. Write the ceiling.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Transport saturation
steps.margin_note: Carriers, all occupied, maximum rate. The word 'all' is the mark.
lines: When ALL the transporters are occupied, the
rate of transport reaches its maximum and
This state is called transport saturation.
steps.why: There is a fixed number of carrier proteins, so once each one is busy the membrane has no spare capacity left however much solute is added outside.
common_mistakes: Saying saturation means transport has stopped. Transport is at its MAXIMUM, not zero.
Leaving out the transporters. The limit exists because their number is fixed.
steps.memory_tip: Every carrier busy means no room for one more.

steps.label: Its effect on facilitated diffusion
steps.margin_note: State the ceiling, then contrast with simple diffusion. The contrast is why the question is asked.

lines.text: Saturation LIMITS the rate; it is a ceiling

lines: Transport saturation sets an upper limit on
Beyond this point, raising the concentration
outside does NOT raise the rate.
Simple diffusion shows no such limit, so
saturation is what tells the two apart.
steps.why: Simple diffusion has no carriers to run out of, so a rate that stops climbing is direct evidence that carriers are involved.
common_mistakes: Writing that saturation increases facilitated diffusion. It LIMITS it. The guide prints the opposite; the ceiling is the correct answer.
Saying simple diffusion also saturates. It does not — it has no carriers.
steps.memory_tip: A full car park does not fill faster because more cars arrive.
